parameters.query:
UPDATE jobs
SET status = CASE WHEN $1 = 'apply' THEN 'approved' ELSE 'skipped' END,
    reviewed_at = now()
WHERE id = $2::bigint AND status = 'pending_review'
RETURNING id, title, company, url, cover_letter, status;

options.systemMessage:
You are Michelle JH, the candidate's job-hunting assistant inside Telegram. The candidate is a junior data analyst in Medellín looking for junior/mid Data Analyst or BI Analyst roles (international remote, or hybrid in Medellín).

How to work:
- Use your tools to answer anything about jobs, scores, statuses or stats. Never invent jobs, numbers, links or statuses: if a tool returns nothing, say so.
- Only change a job's status when the candidate explicitly asks for that specific job. After a change, confirm what changed.
- Reply in the language the candidate writes in (Spanish or English), briefly, in plain text without markdown tables. Use short lines and a few emojis at most.
- When listing jobs, show: job ID, title, company, score and status.
- Status meanings: found = new, filtered_out = rejected by rules or AI, scored = scored, tailored = CV ready, pending_review = sent to Telegram, approved = the candidate chose to apply, skipped = the candidate skipped it, applied, interview, rejected, offer.

parameters.toolDescription: Overview of the job pipeline: number of jobs and average score per status, plus jobs found in the last 24 hours.
List jobs filtered by status and minimum score, best first. Use status 'any' for all statuses.
parameters.query:
SELECT id, title, company, location, work_mode, match_score, status, found_at::date AS found
FROM jobs
WHERE ($1 = 'any' OR status = $1)
  AND coalesce(match_score, 0) >= $2::numeric
ORDER BY match_score DESC NULLS LAST, found_at DESC
LIMIT least(greatest(round($3::numeric)::int, 1), 20);

parameters.toolDescription: Full details of one job by its ID: link, score, matched and missing skills, red flags, AI reasoning, why it was filtered, salary, review fixes and dates.
parameters.query:
SELECT id, title, company, location, work_mode, url, status, match_score, score_confidence,
       matched_skills, missing_skills, red_flags, match_reasoning, filter_reason,
       salary_min, salary_max, salary_currency, salary_period, publisher,
       cv_file_name, tailored_cv->'checks' AS review_fixes, found_at, reviewed_at, applied_at
FROM jobs
WHERE id = $1::bigint;

parameters.toolDescription: Change the status of ONE job, only when the candidate explicitly asks. Allowed statuses: approved, skipped, applied, interview, rejected, offer. Returns nothing if the status is not allowed or the job does not exist.
parameters.query:
UPDATE jobs
SET status = $2::text,
    applied_at = CASE WHEN $2::text = 'applied' THEN now() ELSE applied_at END
WHERE id = $1::bigint
  AND $2::text IN ('approved', 'skipped', 'applied', 'interview', 'rejected', 'offer')
RETURNING id, title, company, status;

parameters.toolDescription: How many status changes happened in the last N days (for example how many jobs were applied to this week).
parameters.query:
SELECT new_status AS status, count(*) AS changes
FROM job_events
WHERE changed_at >= now() - (round($1::numeric)::int * interval '1 day')
GROUP BY new_status
ORDER BY changes DESC;
